paragraphs: GitHub never sleeps and today's trending list is absolutely stacked. If you love discovering open source projects before everyone else, smash that like button, subscribe for weekly GitHub trends, and let's jump straight into 29 trending open-source projects on GitHub. Trending today, episode 15.

TinyPDF is a minimal PDF creation library that does one thing extremely well. This entire library is under 400 lines of code, weighs just 3.3 kilobytes, has zero dependencies, and still generates real standards-compliant PDFs. Compared to something like JSPDF, TinyPDF is nearly 70 times smaller because it intentionally cuts everything you don't need, just the 95% use case, putting text and images on a page.

Ever wish your code could manage itself, but smarter? Meet Conductor, a Gemini CLI extension that brings context-driven development to your projects. It doesn't just write code. It turns your CLI into a proactive project manager. Every feature, every bug fix follows a strict protocol. Context, spec, and plan implement. Keep style guides, tech choices, and product goals consistent.

Qwen Image Layered, a really exciting project pushing image editing in a much more fundamental direction. Instead of treating an image as a single flat output, Qwen Image Layered can decompose an image into multiple RGBA layers. Similar to how designers work in tools like Photoshop or Figma, this layered representation gives you inherent editability. Each layer can be resized, repositioned, or recolored independently.

Ovim, a Mac OS tool that brings systemwide Vim key bindings to every app on your machine. Ovim gives you a true modal editing experience across Mac OS and it does this using two powerful modes depending on how deep you want to go. It intercepts your keystrokes and translates Vim motions into native Mac OS key events so you get instant modal navigation and editing inside any app.

Lightron is a lightweight training framework for large language models. Lightron is designed to sit right in the sweet spot between tiny educational implementations and full-blown production-scale systems. It's clean and modern without sacrificing serious distributed capabilities. Lightron supports full 4D parallelism, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, data parallelism, and context parallelism, all in under 1,000 lines of core code. Ever wish you could talk to the past?

Meet History LLMs, time-locked language models trained entirely on historical texts. Ask about 1913 or 1946, and get answers as people of that era actually thought. Unlike modern AI, these models don't roleplay. They embody the textual culture of their time, from newspapers to novels. Curious what educated Europeans worried about before WWI? History LLMs will tell you in their own words.

AI companies are scraping everyone's blogs for training data. And if you're self-hosting, you basically have no defense. That's where Fuzzy Canary comes in. It's a poor man's anti-scraping trick that plants invisible links in your HTML. Links that trigger AI companies' content safety filters. Yeah, those kinds of sites. Scrapers see the page, panic, and hopefully drop your content. Just install it, add one line, and you're done.

NitroGen, an open foundation model built for generalist gaming agents. NitroGen takes raw pixel input directly from games and predicts gamepad actions, making it game-agnostic and capable of operating across completely different environments. NitroGen uses behavior cloning on what's currently the largest video action gameplay dataset, assembled entirely from gameplay videos found on the internet.

ClaudeBar is a Mac OS menu bar app for anyone using AI coding assistance daily. ClaudeBar lets you monitor your AI usage quotas at a glance all from the menu bar. It supports multiple providers in one place including Claude, Codeex, and Gemini. You get real-time quota tracking across sessions, weekly limits, and even model-specific usage. So there are no surprises when you hit a cap mid-workday.

GitHub Yule Log is a GitHub CLI extension that turns your terminal into a festive animated Yule log fireplace. Yes, inside your terminal. Instead of staring at plain Git logs, you're now reviewing commits while watching a cozy fire crackle. Perfect with a coffee, tea, or something stronger. No productivity claims, no dashboards, just a warm terminal, a burning log, and your Git history glowing in the background.

TailwindSQL. And this one is different. TailwindSQL lets you write SQL queries using Tailwind-style class names directly inside React Server components. Instead of writing raw SQL strings, you class name your way to database queries. It's built specifically for modern React. Zero client-side JavaScript, zero runtime overhead, and queries are parsed and executed at build or render time.

Get Shit Done or GSD, a spec-driven development system built specifically for clawed code. If you've ever tried vibe coding and ended up with fragile code that falls apart the moment things get complex, this project exists to fix exactly that. GSD acts as a context engineering layer. You describe what you want to build and the system extracts, structures, and manages all the context Claude needs before any code gets written.

Poof is a fast, non-blocking alternative to rm -rf. If you've ever waited forever for a huge directory to delete, poof is here to save your time. Instead of blocking your shell while removing files, it instantly moves them out of the way and cleans them up in the background. From your perspective, the deletion is practically instant. On a large filesystem like 4.7 GB with 190,000 files, Poof returns control in about 6 seconds.

CoverFlow Finder, a beautiful Mac OS file browser that brings back the classic CoverFlow experience from the early days of Finder. If you miss that iconic 3D carousel view, complete with smooth animations and reflections, this project delivers it in a modern, polished way. It supports multiple view modes, including CoverFlow and even dual-pane and quadpane layouts, which are fantastic for power users managing lots of files.

GitStory takes your entire GitHub year and transforms it into a cinematic Instagram-story style experience. Just enter a GitHub username and suddenly your commits aren't just numbers, they're a story. You get animated slides showing your total commits, longest streaks, busiest coding days, and even how fast you code over time. Instead of boring charts, GitStory visualizes your tech stack beautifully.

DVGT, short for driving visual geometry transformer, is a universal framework for autonomous driving perception. DVGT can directly predict metric-scaled global 3D point maps from a sequence of unposed multiview images removing the need for post alignment with lidar or other external data. It decodes dense globally consistent geometry in the ego coordinate system producing high-fidelity reconstructions.

Particulate, a feed-forward system for 3D object articulation. Give it a single static 3D mesh of an everyday object and it instantly infers all aspects of the object's articulated structure, including its 3D parts, kinematic hierarchy, and motion constraints. The model is ultra-fast, recovering a fully articulated 3D object in about 10 seconds with just a single forward pass.

Design OS. The problem it solves is common. AI coding tools are fast, but they often miss your intended design. You describe what you want, the AI builds it, and suddenly the UI looks generic, features are half-baked, and you spend as much time correcting as building. Design OS fixes this by separating design from code, guiding you through a structured process that captures what you're building and why.

Ludus FastMCP, an AI-powered management framework for Ludus Cyber Ranges. FastMCP acts as an MCP server, giving you the ability to control and automate cyber range environments using natural language commands. The server exposes 157 tools across 15 modules, covering everything from range life-cycle management and scenario deployment to template creation and CM integration.

Jellyfin Bazarr plugin, a seamless way to manage subtitles directly from Jellyfin. Normally, you'd have to switch over to Bazarr's web interface to search and download subtitles, but this plugin brings that functionality right into Jellyfin's native subtitle UI. It fully supports both movies and TV episodes with features designed for convenience and speed. If you want on-demand subtitles without leaving Jellyfin, this plugin makes it effortless.

Keyden is a clean and elegant TOTP authenticator built right into your Mac OS menu bar. Keyden lets you securely store your two-factor authentication secrets in the Mac OS keychain and gives you one-click access to your verification codes. Adding accounts is easy via QR code scanning and you can even import multiple accounts in batch or migrate from Google Authenticator.

WorldCanvas, a framework that lets you paint promptable world events using text, trajectories, and reference images. Think of it as an image-to-video simulation engine that gives you control over object movements and scene evolution. WorldCanvas combines three key modalities: trajectories to encode motion, timing, and visibility, natural language for semantic intent, reference images to preserve object identity and appearance.

Chatery WhatsApp, a WhatsApp API backend built with Express.js and the Bailey's library. This project is designed for developers who want full programmatic control over WhatsApp with support for multiple simultaneous sessions so you can manage several WhatsApp accounts from a single backend. It provides real-time WebSocket events giving you instant updates for incoming messages and other activity as it happens.

JustJSHTML, a dependency-free JavaScript HTML5 parser that works in both browsers and Node.js. JustJSHTML is a full JavaScript port of the Python project just HTML, aiming to pass the complete HTML5 lib test suite, including tokenization and serialization without relying on any runtime dependencies. If you need a minimal HTML5 parser in JavaScript without the bloat, JustJSHTML is a sleek, efficient solution.

Gazetteer is a fully offline boundary-based reverse geocoding library written in Python. Instead of guessing the nearest point like traditional geocoders, Gazetteer validates coordinates inside real administrative boundaries, giving you far more accurate results, especially near borders. It supports up to three administrative levels, country, state, and cities or districts covering 210 countries and over 145,000 boundaries.

What if a robot could learn movement just by watching a video? Video2Robot is an end-to-end pipeline that converts videos or even AI-generated clips from Sora or Veo directly into humanoid robot motions. It starts with human pose extraction, tracking body joints frame by frame, then automatically converts those movements into robot-compatible motion commands.

MacPersistenceChecker is a native Mac OS security tool that scans every persistence mechanism on your system, launch agents, daemons, and more. It doesn't just list them; it verifies code signatures, tracks when items appeared, and shows you what stays and why it matters. This makes it incredibly useful for spotting malware or suspicious background services you didn't install or forgot about.

LLM-TradeBot. Before asking how to trade, it asks if it should trade at all. This is a multi-agent AI trading system built on an adversarial decision framework. Four specialized agents constantly challenge each other before any position is taken. It analyzes multiple time frames in parallel, detects market regimes, understands price position, and dynamically recalibrates confidence in real-time.

Lumina Energy Card. An ultra-modern 3D Lovelace card that turns your electricity data into a cinematic experience. You get animated energy flows for your home load, grid, solar, batteries, and even EV charging. All moving in real-time with customizable colors, speeds, and styles. Lumina supports up to six PV sensors, plus four battery systems with smart smoothing and liquid-fill visuals.
